name: has_flag
reason: One-line mirror; HasFlagSpec proves for all UInt32 that has_flag holds exactly when every bit of flag is set in curr, which pins the function completely.

name: iscallstmt
reason: Mirror of the isa test and the four head comparisons; proven for every input that it is false for a non-Expr and true exactly for the heads :call, :invoke, :foreigncall and :foreignglobal, a full characterization.

name: flags_for_effects
reason: Mirror of the nine conditional ors in source order; proven for every Effects that each of the ten defined effect bits is set exactly when its query (or the EFIIMO/RSIIMO else-branch condition) holds and no non-effect flag is set; only never-read undefined bits (7-9, 11, 12, 15, 21-31) are left unpinned.

name: inlining_cost
reason: No entry states the cost it returns: the clauses only compare it with MAX_INLINE_COST, so a function returning 0 for every finite cost passes, and the UInt8 case (CodeInstance.inferred can be a bare cost byte) and the MAX_INLINE_COST fallback for other sources are never stated.

name: is_inlineable
reason: Pinned only for compressed sources (byte != 0xff) and for CodeInfo costs produced by the clamp or set_inlineable!; the bare UInt8 cost byte and non-source inputs such as nothing (both reach it from typeinfer.jl:1256) are never stated, so is_inlineable(nothing) == true would pass.

name: set_inlineable!
reason: Proven that after set_inlineable!(src, val) both the CodeInfo and its compressed form give is_inlineable == val, which is what the function exists for; the exact MIN_INLINE_COST stored is only observable through that test.

name: inline_cost_clamp
reason: Proven for every Int (via exhaustive kernel checks over all UInt16 and UInt8 that are stated as lemmas, not bounds on the claim): range 10:65535, monotone, idempotent, x <= clamp(x) <= 33x/32 on 10:3968 and survives the 8-bit encoding, which leaves almost no freedom; the refuted 3969 -> MAX_INLINE_COST case has a reproducer and arises in real compilation only with inline_cost_threshold above 3968, which GPUCompiler's typemax(Int) setting gives.

name: is_declared_inline
reason: The only clause says the compressed and uncompressed forms agree, so a function that always returns false passes; the result is never tied to the inlining field being SRC_FLAG_DECLARED_INLINE.

name: is_declared_noinline
reason: The only clause says the compressed and uncompressed forms agree, so a function that always returns false passes; the result is never tied to the inlining field being SRC_FLAG_DECLARED_NOINLINE.

name: src_inlining_policy
reason: The method-instance method is pinned for every input: false when the method has a generator it cannot invoke, otherwise exactly the source method's answer; the callsite-annotations entry adds the @inline/@noinline consequences.

name: src_inlining_policy
reason: Every Src constructor is covered by an equation (OptimizationState unwrapped, IRCode true, UInt8 and other false, CodeInfo and String equal to is_stmt_inline(flag) || cost != MAX_INLINE_COST), a full characterization in terms of its callees.

name: is_stmt_inline
reason: The clauses only say the result ignores bits disjoint from IR_FLAG_INLINE and is true once that bit is set, so the constant-true function passes; is_stmt_inline(0) == false or an iff with bit 1 is never stated.

name: is_stmt_noinline
reason: The clauses only say the result ignores bits disjoint from IR_FLAG_NOINLINE and is true once that bit is set, so the constant-true function passes; is_stmt_noinline(0) == false or an iff with bit 2 is never stated.

name: plus_saturate
reason: Not stated alone, but the closed form of inline_cost_model pins it on every input the loop gives it (body cost below a threshold < 2^62, statement cost up to 2^62+3 or typemax(Int) for a try), where wrapping addition or plain max would fail; the non-saturating case the note gives (typemax(Int)-1 plus 5) needs a body cost no real loop reaches before its early exit.

name: statement_cost
reason: The entries state only bounds (0:2^62+3, non-negative) and no-throw, plus two refutations, so a function returning 0 for every well-formed statement and BoundsError for a one-argument typeassert satisfies all of them; no clause pins any cost (0 for getfield/tuple, 1 or the penalty for memoryref ops, 20 for foreigncall, 100 for copyast, the intrinsic halving); the refuted typeassert (user code calling Core.typeassert(x)) and llvmcall (every llvmcall) inputs both arise in real compilation and have reproducers.

name: statement_or_branch_cost
reason: Only the try case (typemax(Int), via EnterNeverInlineable) is pinned; the bounds entry's prop is about statement_cost and sobc_nonneg is a lemma, so a function charging 0 for backward branches passes; the 40-per-backward-branch rule and the IRCode block lookup are never stated.

name: inline_cost_model
reason: The closed form pins it exactly (MAX_INLINE_COST when the exact sum of the statement costs exceeds the threshold, else the clamp of the sum) with the bounds penalty <= 2^62 and threshold < 2^62 in the statement; append-monotonicity and order independence are proven on top, and the try case for any threshold below typemax(Int).

name: statement_costs!
reason: The returned maximum is pinned, but the per-line costs are tied to the body only through their sum in the inline_cost_model closed form, so a function that writes the whole sum to cost[1] and zeros elsewhere passes; cost[line] == statement_or_branch_cost(stmt, line) is never stated.
